lesson.child_mission: Writing a letter to the editor means a formal greeting, clear position, evidenced reasons and a respectful close with your name.
lesson.evidence_instructions: Save the independent response, specific revisions and both short-answer explanations; record oral evidence for speaking tasks.
lesson.extension: Apply the same strategy to an unfamiliar topic or audience, then compare the effect of two different choices.
lesson.guided_practice:
PRACTISE BEFORE READING THE FEEDBACK
Order: greeting; ask; reason; evidence; close.

FEEDBACK
Greeting → position → reasons/evidence → respectful close/name.

CHECK
Insulting the editor or public ends persuasion.
lesson.independent_task:
INDEPENDENT EVIDENCE
Write a 160–200 word letter to the editor with formal features, two evidenced reasons and a calm request.

Write a short reflection describing one specific revision you made and why.
lesson.learning_intention: Writing a letter to the editor means a formal greeting, clear position, evidenced reasons and a respectful close with your name.
lesson.offline_alternative: Use paper and pencil to complete the original task, then retain a photograph or short parent observation as evidence.
lesson.parent_notes:
Parent: Marking guidance for the independent task: Write a 160–200 word letter to the editor with formal features, two evidenced reasons and a calm request. Accept equivalent original responses that show the same skill.

Parent: Written model 1: Sample: original example using letter on new material; names a specific word, source or choice and explains its effect.

Parent: Written model 2: Sample error: Insulting the editor or public ends persuasion.. Correction: Greeting → position → reasons/evidence → respectful close/name.. Why it helps the audience is stated.

Parent: Likely misconception: Insulting the editor or public ends persuasion. Keep sample answers out of the child role.

Parent: Short-answer focus 1: Produce a fresh example demonstrating letter on new material (not the worked model). Explain the particular words, sources or choices that make it work.

Parent: Short-answer focus 2: Name one likely error with letter, correct it, and explain why the correction helps a reader or audience.

Parent: Marking notes: Accept original work about letter with a specific supporting detail. Reject copied model wording with no new material. / Accept a misconception, a correction, and a purpose-linked reason for letter. Reject corrections that do not change the inaccurate idea..

teach_steps.explain:
Writing a letter to the editor means a formal greeting, clear position, evidenced reasons and a respectful close with your name.

WHY IT MATTERS
This helps the learner make decisions based on specific language evidence, rather than guess or copy someone else. Keep the meaning accurate and explain the choice.

HOW TO WORK
Read the original example and locate the words or actions that support the idea. Before looking at the correction, make your own attempt using the exact question provided. Check your response against the feedback: did you address the same skill and show your reasoning? If a detail is uncertain, identify what would have to be checked. One deliberate, justified revision is more useful than making the answer longer.
